summary: @servicetitan/assist-ui preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (_0x-style identifiers and dictionary-object indirection around execFileSync calls). During npm install it checks for Bun on PATH and, if absent, downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts and chmod +x's the bun binary, then execs that binary against a sibling file math_init.js from the package directory. math_init.js is a 727KB, single-line, heavily obfuscated Bun bundle (// @bun @bun-cjs header, string-array rotation via WV8StW(MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift())), multi-thousand-entry constant table decoded through String.fromCodePoint). The package is published as a React UI component library, which has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime or execute an opaque bundled payload during installation. The obfuscation of both the loader and the executed payload, together with the alternate-runtime execution path that bypasses Node-only tracing, are consistent with a deliberate install-time dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
